findings.issue_text: [BUG] The migration dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'] on a query that returns zero rows on any database where the embed_category site setting was never overridden, crashing db:migrate with NoMethodError on nil. Discourse persists only non-default site settings, so virtually every existing forum (and any fresh db:migrate) has no embed_category row; the INNER JOIN returns nothing, [0] is nil, and the deploy's migration aborts — the `if category_id == 0` fallback written for exactly this case is unreachable behind the crash, and CI never catches it because the test DB is built from schema.rb, not by running this migration.

[BUG] Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update passes the nil returned by the id lookup straight into save_host, which calls nil.host= and raises NoMethodError. An admin who saves an edit after another admin (or another tab) already deleted that host receives a 500 with an internal-server-error popup instead of a 404 or a rendered validation error.

[BUG] Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy calls host.destroy on the nil returned by the id lookup when the record is already gone, raising NoMethodError. Two admins deleting the same host (or a double-submit racing the first DELETE) makes the second request return a 500 instead of success_json, surfacing an error popup in the admin UI for an operation that actually succeeded.

[BUG] The save handler overwrites host.category with Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')), which returns undefined when no category was chosen, discarding the category the server actually assigned in its response. The first-use flow (add host, type a hostname, save without picking a category — cantSave only requires the hostname) renders the saved row with a blank category badge even though the server stored Uncategorized, and re-editing it shows an empty chooser until a full page reload.

[ADVISORY] The update action is a silent no-op: it re-renders the embedding without reading params or persisting anything, and the saveChanges action in admin-embedding.js.es6 that calls embedding.update({}) has no trigger in any template. PUT /admin/customize/embedding returns 200 success while changing nothing, so the next developer who wires a save button to the existing saveChanges action, or any API client that PUTs embedding changes, ships a feature that silently fails to save.

[ADVISORY] The fabricator definitions are swapped between files: category_fabricator.rb now contains only Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while all four category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category) moved into the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Everything still loads because fabricators are glob-loaded so no spec fails, but the next maintainer editing or searching for the category fabricators is sent to the wrong file, and any future merge or file-scoped tooling around these files inherits the misplacement.

[BUG] The host format validation accepts port-suffixed values like 'example.com:8080', but record_for_host compares against URI(...).host ('example.com'), which never equals the stored 'example.com:8080'. An admin who enters a host with a port gets a record that validates and saves cleanly yet authorizes no referer — every embed request from that host is rejected with Discourse::InvalidAccess and TopicEmbed.import falls back to no category, with nothing in the UI indicating why.

[ADVISORY] EmbeddableHost has no uniqueness validation on host, so the same host can be saved twice with different categories, and record_for_host resolves it with an unordered where(...).first. An admin who re-adds an existing host (the UI does not prevent it) gets embeds posting to whichever duplicate row the database returns first — an effectively arbitrary category that can silently change between requests.

[ADVISORY] The only specs added for the new admin controllers assert the class's ancestry; no test in the diff issues a request against EmbeddableHostsController create/update/destroy, the uncategorized_category_id fallback, or the migration's data migration. The P0 migration crash and both nil-host 500s in this PR ship undetected — CI builds the test DB from schema.rb so the data migration never runs, and the controller specs never exercise a request, so a regression in save_host or the migration breaks production upgrades with zero test failures.

[ADVISORY] Embed authorization switched from reading the process-cached SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts value to EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?, which issues an unindexed lower(host) = ? SQL query on every request. Every page view of every page embedding this forum's comments now costs a database round-trip on the public embed path that previously served from the settings cache, adding DB load proportional to embed traffic (and the migration creates no index on host).

[ADVISORY] The rewritten 'find embedded' test requests store.find('fruit', 2) but the pretender's /fruits/:id handler ignores :id and returns fruits[0], so the test asserts apple's color ids [1,2] while the fixture it names (banana) declares color_ids [3]. The test passes only because of the handler's quirk and documents false hydration behavior; the next developer who fixes the pretender to honor :id or edits banana's fixture data breaks this test in a way that reads as a store regression rather than a test-authoring mistake.

[BUG] The migration dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'] on a query that returns zero rows on any install where the embed_category site setting was never changed from its default, raising NoMethodError on nil before the category_id == 0 fallback can run. db:migrate aborts with NoMethodError on fresh installs and on the majority of existing installs (Discourse only persists site settings that differ from their YAML default, and embed_category's default is ''), blocking every deploy and every new-install bootstrap; the `if category_id == 0` fallback on line 14 is dead code because the crash fires in exactly the missing-row case it was written to handle.

[BUG] The migration inserts old embeddable_hosts setting values verbatim ('#{h}') without applying the model's scheme/path-stripping normalization, so rows like 'http://eviltrout.com' or 'https://example.com/1234' can never match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host's comparison of lower(host) against URI(...).host. Every existing install whose hosts were stored with a scheme prefix or a path — formats the deleted SiteSetting spec explicitly supported and tested ('works with a http host', 'https://example.com/1234') — gets 'invalid referer host' 403s on all embedded pages immediately after upgrade, silently, until an admin manually edits and re-saves each row; no spec in the diff exercises migration-produced data (the model specs only use fabricated, normalized hosts).

[BUG] update passes EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first to save_host with no nil guard, so a nonexistent id makes save_host call nil.host= and raise NoMethodError, returning a 500. An admin who saves a host another admin just deleted (stale tab), or any PUT to a dead id, receives a raw 500 exception instead of the 404 the REST resource contract implies.

[BUG] destroy calls host.destroy on EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first with no nil guard, so destroying an already-destroyed host raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500. A double-confirm race or two admins deleting the same host makes the second DELETE return a 500 instead of success/404, and the client's unhandled rejection leaves the row rendered with no feedback.

[ADVISORY] The only spec added for the new controller asserts ancestry (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController); no spec in the diff posts to create, update, or destroy, so the blank-category fallback to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id, the render_json_error path, and the unguarded record lookups are never executed under test (embedding_controller_spec.rb is likewise ancestry-only). The nil-record 500s and the malformed-payload 500s in this controller ship completely unverified — the first request spec written would have caught them — and a regression in the uncategorized fallback would silently mis-categorize every host saved without a category with no test failing.

[BUG] save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host][:host] and params[:embeddable_host][:category_id] with no presence guard, so a payload missing the embeddable_host key (or carrying host: null) crashes with NoMethodError — in the controller, or in the model's before_validation nil.sub! — instead of returning a 422. Any API or script caller hitting the new REST resource without a well-formed embeddable_host payload (the shipped UI always sends both keys) receives a 500 rather than the render_json_error 4xx that the invalid-host path promises.

[BUG] The validation regex explicitly permits port-bearing entries ((:[0-9]{1,5})?) but record_for_host compares lower(host) to URI(...).host, which never contains a port, so a host saved as 'example.com:8080' validates, persists, and can never authorize any referer. An admin who enters a host with a port — accepted by both the regex and the UI — gets permanent 'invalid referer host' 403s for that host with nothing pointing at the port as the cause; the new model specs cover http/https/path trimming but never the port case.

[ADVISORY] record_for_host issues WHERE lower(host) = ? on every embed request (embed_controller#ensure_embeddable and TopicRetriever#invalid_host? both call it per request), replacing the previous in-memory SiteSetting check, and the migration creates no index on host — which the lower() comparison would bypass anyway. Every embedded-comments pageview on a host site now costs an unindexed DB roundtrip that the old code served from the cached settings store; high-traffic embeds multiply database load on a hot path the diff previously served from cache.

[ADVISORY] Nothing enforces uniqueness of embeddable_hosts.host (no uniqueness validation and no unique index in the migration), and record_for_host selects .first with no ORDER BY. An admin who adds the same host twice with different categories gets duplicate rows in the embedding table, and which category newly imported embedded topics land in is whichever row Postgres happens to return first — a silent, unpredictable category assignment.

[ADVISORY] belongs_to :category declares no dependent option and the migration adds no foreign key, so deleting a category that an embeddable host references leaves the row with a dangling category_id. After a routine category deletion, new embedded topics for that host fail (PostCreator rejects the dead category_id and TopicEmbed.create! raises inside the feed-poll job) with no admin-visible error, the embedding page renders a blank category badge, and editing that host silently resets it to Uncategorized because the empty chooser sends no category_id.

[ADVISORY] The format regex requires a dotted TLD (\.[a-z]{2,5}), so bare hostnames like 'localhost' or 'intranet' that the old free-text setting accepted and matched fail validation. An intranet or dev install embedding from a non-dotted host can no longer save the host at all — the old code matched such entries through its string fallback — and a migrated bare-hostname row keeps working but becomes uneditable, since any save of it now fails validation.

[ADVISORY] The update action ignores params entirely and re-renders the serialized embedding while returning 200, persisting nothing, and its client twin saveChanges in admin-embedding.js.es6 is never rendered by embedding.hbs. PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a silent no-op on a live admin surface: any caller — or a future template wiring the already-written saveChanges action — believes changes were saved when nothing was written; the action pair should be deleted or implemented.

[BUG] On save success the component overwrites host.category with Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')), which returns undefined when no category was chosen, clobbering whatever the server response hydrated. An admin who saves a new host without picking a category (the save button is enabled as soon as a hostname is typed) sees a blank category badge even though the server stored Uncategorized, and believes the category was not saved until a full page reload.

[ADVISORY] destroyRecord().then() has no .catch, unlike the save action's popupAjaxError, so a rejected DELETE becomes an unhandled promise rejection. When the server rejects the delete (the nil-host 500 on a double delete, an expired session, a 403), the admin has already confirmed the bootbox dialog, nothing happens, no error popup appears, and the row silently stays — indistinguishable from a broken button.

[ADVISORY] The diff swaps the two fabricator files' contents: Fabricator(:embeddable_host) now lives in category_fabricator.rb while all four category fabricators (category, diff_category, happy_category, private_category) moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, whose blob hash (a37f5b4c8ba) is the old category file's. The next maintainer adding or editing a category fabricator opens category_fabricator.rb and finds the embeddable_host fabricator instead; fabricator changes land in misleadingly named files and future review diffs for category changes point at the wrong file.

[BUG] The embed_category lookup executes `[0]['id']` on a query result that is empty whenever the embed_category site setting row is absent or its value matches no category name, so `db:migrate` raises NoMethodError (undefined method `[]` for nil) and aborts the deploy. Every existing install that never explicitly set embed_category — and every fresh install, where the row cannot exist — fails this migration and cannot upgrade; the uncategorized fallback at lines 14-16 is unreachable because the crash preempts it and the join can never return id 0.

[BUG] update and destroy assign `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without a nil check and then call save_host(nil) / nil.destroy, so a request for a nonexistent host id raises NoMethodError and returns 500 instead of 404. An admin saving a row that another admin just deleted (or any API call with a stale id) gets a 500 surfaced via popupAjaxError instead of a clean not-found response.

[ADVISORY] The fabricator files are content-swapped: category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while all four category fabricators (category, diff_category, happy_category, private_category) live in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, whose blob (a37f5b4c8ba) is byte-identical to the old category_fabricator.rb. Developers navigating by filename edit the wrong file for both fabricators, the category fabricators' git history is now attached to the embeddable_host file, and future cleanup or review of category fabricators gets misdirected.

[ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update reads no params and re-renders the unchanged OpenStruct, and the client saveChanges action that PUTs to /admin/customize/embedding is invoked by no template in the diff, making the entire PUT pipeline inert work not traceable to the host/category editing requirement. Dead admin API surface: any future client that PUTs embedding settings receives a 200 while nothing is persisted — a silent no-op trap — and saveChanges sits in the controller as unreachable code.

[ADVISORY] EmbeddableHost has no uniqueness validation or unique index on host while record_for_host resolves duplicates with `.first` under no ORDER BY, so the category applied to new embeds is undefined when the same host is stored twice. An admin who enters the same host twice with different categories — the UI and validation both permit it — gets feed-embedded topics posted to an unpredictable one of the two categories.

[ADVISORY] The host validation regex explicitly permits a `:port` suffix (and a path), but record_for_host matches against `URI(...).host`, which excludes the port, so a host stored as `example.com:3000` can never match any referer. An admin (typically a developer embedding from localhost:3000) saves a host the UI accepts as valid and embedding silently never works, with no error at save or request time; the `(\/.*)?` alternative is additionally dead because before_validation strips paths.

[ADVISORY] The only spec for the new Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts ancestry, so create/update/destroy behavior — param handling, the blank-category-to-uncategorized fallback in save_host, and error rendering — is exercised by no test in the diff. A regression in save_host (e.g., the nil-record 500 or a broken uncategorized fallback) breaks the new admin embedding UI while the suite stays green.

[ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable now calls EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer), which runs a `where("lower(host) = ?")` database query on every embed/comments request where the previous check read the memory-cached SiteSetting with no database access. Sites with embedded comments add an unindexed database query to every blog page view that loads the comments iframe, turning a previously zero-DB hot path into a per-request database hit.

[ADVISORY] expandable_first_post? drops the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` guard, so the invariant 'no expandable first post unless embedding is configured' is no longer enforced. An admin who deletes all embeddable hosts to decommission embedding loses the global kill switch the old setting provided — previously-embedded topics keep rendering truncated expandable first posts — and the retained spec named 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer sets anything blank, so it passes while verifying nothing about the removed gate.

[BUG] The host format validation explicitly permits port-bearing entries (`:[0-9]{1,5}`) and before_validation preserves the port, but record_for_host compares the stored value against `URI(...).host`, which never contains a port, so a host saved as 'example.com:8080' passes validation and can then never match any referer. An admin who whitelists an origin served on a non-standard port gets 'Discourse::InvalidAccess: invalid referer host' on every embed request from that origin — the embedding feature is silently dead for that host even though the admin UI accepted and stored the entry (the write path and the compare path disagree on canonical form).

[BUG] The embeddable_hosts table is created with no UNIQUE index on host and EmbeddableHost declares no uniqueness validation, so the same host — including case variants like 'EvilTrout.com' vs 'eviltrout.com', since writes are never case-normalized — can be stored in multiple rows. record_for_host resolves duplicates via `.first` (lowest id), so when an admin edits the category on the newer duplicate row the change is silently ignored and embedded topics keep posting to the older row's category; the admin UI also renders two indistinguishable rows with no error.

[BUG] EmbeddableHost declares belongs_to :category with no FK constraint in the migration and no dependent cleanup anywhere in the diff, so deleting a category leaves embeddable_hosts rows pointing at a nonexistent category_id. TopicEmbed.import then passes the dead category_id into PostCreator (which runs with skip_validations: true), so embedded-topic creation for that host produces topics in a nonexistent category or fails outright, and the admin UI renders a blank category cell because Discourse.Category.findById returns undefined.

[BUG] before_validation calls `self.host.sub!` with no nil guard and the model declares no presence validation, so saving a record whose host attribute is nil raises NoMethodError before the format validation can produce an error. A staff request to POST/PUT /admin/embeddable_hosts whose embeddable_host params omit `host` returns a 500 (NoMethodError on nil.sub!) instead of the 4xx validation error the render_json_error branch exists to return.

[ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update ignores the request body and persists nothing — it re-renders the exact state the fetch_embedding before_filter already loaded — while the frontend saveChanges action sends `embedding.update({})` against it. PUT /admin/customize/embedding returns 200 success while saving nothing, so the first client that PUTs real payload data silently loses it; the saveChanges action is additionally dead code since no element in embedding.hbs triggers it.

[ADVISORY] The new plural branch of _hydrateEmbedded calls `obj[k].map` with no null check and overwrites `obj[pluralize(subType)]` unconditionally — with no per-element guard, unlike the singular branch's `if (hydrated)` — in a store method that runs for every model hydration, not just embedding. Any payload whose `foo_ids` value is null crashes hydration with a TypeError on null.map, and any payload whose id list references a record missing from the side-load silently loses the raw ids and gains undefined array entries, breaking every consumer of that model; no test in the diff exercises the lookup-miss case the singular branch's guard was written for.

[ADVISORY] The fabricator files are content-swapped: category_fabricator.rb now defines only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while all four category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category) were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Fabrication loads files by glob so the suite still passes, but the next developer who edits or deletes embeddable_host_fabricator.rb (believing it holds the embeddable host fabricator) removes the category fabricators and breaks the entire spec suite, and anyone searching for the :category definition is sent to the wrong file.

[ADVISORY] The only spec covering Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts class inheritance and never exercises create, update, destroy, or save_host. The guard is a pure proxy that stays green no matter what the actions do — any regression in the new CRUD surface (the uncategorized defaulting, the error rendering, a mistyped params key) passes CI and ships to the first staff user in production.

[ADVISORY] The referer check on the embed/comments hot path changed from a cached in-process SiteSetting read to an unconditional per-request SQL query — EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? runs `where("lower(host) = ?")` against a column with no index. Every render of an embedded comments iframe now adds a database roundtrip (a non-sargable full scan) where the previous check cost zero DB reads, adding load that scales with embed traffic on popular sites.

[ADVISORY] The host format regex requires a dotted TLD of exactly 2-5 letters (`\.[a-z]{2,5}`), rejecting dotless hostnames like 'localhost' or 'intranet' and valid 6-character TLDs like '.museum'. An admin whose embedding origin is a dotless internal hostname or a long-TLD domain cannot whitelist it — the save is rejected with a format error and there is no workaround short of the development-mode admin bypass.

[BUG] The migration raises NoMethodError on nil because `execute(...)[0]` is nil when the `embed_category` setting has no site_settings row or its value no longer matches a category name, and the `if category_id == 0` fallback to uncategorized_category_id is unreachable dead code (Postgres category ids are never 0 and the crash happens before the branch). Every fresh install and every existing site that never customized embed_category fails `db:migrate` with `undefined method '[]' for nil:NilClass`, blocking the entire deploy; the written intent — default migrated hosts to the uncategorized category — is never executed.

[BUG] The migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts setting entries verbatim via raw SQL, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation scheme/path stripping, so entries like `http://eviltrout.com` — which the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` explicitly accepted (it stripped the scheme before comparing, per the specs this diff deletes) — are stored with the `http://` prefix intact. After upgrade, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against the bare referer host from `uri.host`, so a migrated `http://example.com` row never matches and every embed request from that host returns InvalidAccess — existing embeds break silently across the site with no error and no migration warning.

[BUG] `update` and `destroy` feed `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` directly into `save_host`/`destroy` with no nil check, so any request for a nonexistent host id raises NoMethodError on nil (`nil.host =` in save_host, `nil.destroy` in destroy). PUT or DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale id (the host was already deleted from another admin session or tab) returns a 500 instead of a 404, and because the client delete flow has no rejection handler the row silently stays in the table.

[ADVISORY] `record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` on every embed request, replacing the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` read that was served from Discourse's per-process settings cache, and the migration creates no index on `host` (which the `lower()` wrap would defeat anyway). Every pageview of every externally embedding site now incurs a per-request sequential-scan DB query on the /embed/comments hot path — externally driven traffic the forum cannot throttle — so database load scales with third-party pageviews where it previously scaled at zero.

[ADVISORY] The fabricator files have their contents swapped: category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while all 27 lines of :category/:diff_category/:happy_category/:private_category fabricators moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb (the new file's blob hash a37f5b4c8ba is identical to the old category_fabricator.rb, proving an accidental swap). Tests keep passing because Fabricator globs the whole directory, but maintainers navigating by filename edit the wrong file, git blame/history for the category fabricators is severed, and a future partial revert or `git mv` of either file silently drops or duplicates fabricator definitions.

[ADVISORY] The `update` action persists nothing — it re-renders the same OpenStruct from fetch_embedding — and its only client caller, `saveChanges` in admin-embedding.js.es6, is triggered by no element in embedding.hbs, leaving the PUT /admin/customize/embedding route and the controller action inert. A future developer wiring embedding-level settings to this page will assume the existing save plumbing works and ship a UI that silently discards user input, because the endpoint returns a success-shaped payload without saving anything.

[ADVISORY] The migration deletes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site-setting rows inside `change` with no down path, destroying the source data irreversibly while `create_table` remains auto-reversible. An operator who rolls back this migration to back out a bad release gets the table dropped but the deleted settings rows are not restored — the site's entire embeddable-host configuration is lost with no recovery path.

[ADVISORY] The validation regex explicitly accepts port-bearing hosts via `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`, but `record_for_host` matches against `uri.host`, which never includes a port, so a stored `example.com:8080` can never equal any referer host. An admin who whitelists `example.com:8080` gets a clean save and then embedding from that host keeps failing with InvalidAccess and no diagnostic — the model accepts input its own matching logic cannot honor.

[ADVISORY] The delete action chains `destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch`, unlike the save action in the same component that handles rejection with popupAjaxError. When the DELETE fails (the 500 from the unguarded nil host in the controller, or a stale-id rejection), the admin gets no feedback and the row remains in the table, so the failure presents as the confirm dialog doing nothing.

[ADVISORY] The only spec for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts subclass ancestry, leaving the new `save_host` logic — the blank-category fallback to uncategorized_category_id, validation-error rendering, and the before_validation host normalization — with no test coverage. A regression in the uncategorized fallback or the error path ships with no failing spec, and embedded topics start posting to the wrong category or the controller returns unrendered 500s on invalid input.

[ADVISORY] `belongs_to :category` has no dependent handling and nothing in the diff or in category deletion cleans up embeddable_hosts rows, leaving dangling category_id values after a category is deleted. Once an admin deletes a category that hosts point at, the embedding table renders a blank category, the next host save silently reassigns the host to uncategorized, and TopicEmbed.import passes the dead category_id to PostCreator for newly embedded topics.

[BUG] The migration string-interpolates each line of the migrated embeddable_hosts site setting directly into a raw SQL INSERT (VALUES ('#{h}', ...)), so a stored value containing a single quote breaks out of the string literal and injects arbitrary SQL. The old embeddable_hosts setting was free-form admin-entered text with no write-side format validation (the removed allows_embeddable_host? only stripped schemes at read time, and the removed specs show values like 'http://discourse.org' being stored), so any value with an apostrophe aborts db:migrate with a PG syntax error and blocks the upgrade; a deliberately crafted setting value (config treated as attacker input) executes attacker-chosen SQL with the migration role's privileges during deploy.

[BUG] update passes the unchecked result of EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first into save_host, so a request whose id matches no row executes nil.host = ... and raises NoMethodError. An admin saving a host that another admin deleted in the meantime (or any direct PUT to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a bogus id) gets a 500 from an unhandled NoMethodError instead of a 404, and the Ember client's save flow surfaces a raw server error.

[BUG] destroy calls host.destroy on the unchecked result of EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first, raising NoMethodError on nil when the id matches no row. A DELETE for an already-removed host (double-click on the trash button racing the first request, or two admins managing hosts simultaneously) returns a 500 instead of success_json/404, rejecting the client's destroyRecord promise and leaving the row stuck in the UI.

[BUG] save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host] without any require/permit guard, so a create or update request whose payload omits the embeddable_host key raises NoMethodError on nil[:host]. Any direct POST/PUT to /admin/embeddable_hosts without the embeddable_host payload (an API consumer or client bug) returns a 500 instead of a 400, logging an unhandled exception on an admin route.

[BUG] The before_validation block calls self.host.sub! with no nil guard, so saving a record whose host attribute is nil raises NoMethodError before validates_format_of can reject the value. Creating a host with an embeddable_host payload that omits the host key (host.host = nil) returns a 500 instead of the 422 validation error that the controller's render_json_error branch is designed to produce.

[ADVISORY] category_id is accepted from params with no existence validation, the new embeddable_hosts table has no foreign key, and nothing clears embeddable_hosts.category_id when a category is deleted, so an EmbeddableHost row can reference a nonexistent category. An admin deletes a category that an embeddable host posts to; every subsequent feed-poll import (TopicEmbed.import passes eh.category_id straight to PostCreator) then creates embedded topics against a category that no longer exists, silently misfiling or breaking those topics.

[BUG] The only test in this new spec asserts `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`, which passes regardless of what the controller's actions do, so create/update/destroy ship with zero behavioral verification. A regression in any controller behavior passes CI: update and destroy crash with NoMethodError (500) when params[:id] matches no EmbeddableHost (nil is passed to save_host/destroy), and the blank-category_id fallback to uncategorized_category_id is never exercised — an admin acting on a stale/deleted row gets an unhandled 500 with no failing test.

[BUG] The only test asserts `Admin::EmbeddingController < Admin::AdminController` and never issues a request, so the show/update serialization contract that the new JS store hydration depends on is completely unverified. The payload shape the new _hydrateEmbedded plural-ids path consumes (root 'embedding' with embeddable_host_ids side-load) has no test — if the serializer emits a shape the store mishandles, the admin embedding page renders an empty hosts table with CI green; the update action, which persists nothing (it only re-renders the OpenStruct built in fetch_embedding), also ships unverified.

[BUG] The restructured expandable_first_post? tests still treat embeddable hosts as a gating input even though this diff removed the host check from the method: the 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false and has_topic_embed? is false on a built topic, and every positive test fabricates an EmbeddableHost the code never reads. The suite cannot detect a regression that re-introduces a host requirement into expandable_first_post? (all positive cases have a host present and the 'blank host' case passes for unrelated reasons), and a reader of the spec concludes hosts still gate the behavior when the code now ignores them entirely.

[ADVISORY] The fabricator definitions were swapped between files: category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb (lines 1-27) holds the :category/:diff_category/:happy_category/:private_category fabricators. [ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update ignores the request body and persists nothing — it re-renders the exact state the fetch_embedding before_filter already loaded — while the frontend saveChanges action sends `embedding.update({})` against it. PUT /admin/customize/embedding returns 200 success while saving nothing, so the first client that PUTs real payload data silently loses it; the saveChanges action is additionally dead code since no element in embedding.hbs triggers it.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` does not read `params` or persist anything; it simply re-serializes `@embedding` created by `fetch_embedding` (an `OpenStruct` with `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`). Yet `config/routes.rb` adds `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`, and the Ember controller defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({})`. This PUT endpoint will return success while ignoring any request body, which is misleading/broken behavior (silent no-op), and the `saveChanges` action appears unused by `embedding.hbs` (no button/action wired).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new plural branch of _hydrateEmbedded calls `obj[k].map` with no null check and overwrites `obj[pluralize(subType)]` unconditionally — with no per-element guard, unlike the singular branch's `if (hydrated)` — in a store method that runs for every model hydration, not just embedding. Any payload whose `foo_ids` value is null crashes hydration with a TypeError on null.map, and any payload whose id list references a record missing from the side-load silently loses the raw ids and gains undefined array entries, breaking every consumer of that model; no test in the diff exercises the lookup-miss case the singular branch's guard was written for.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, the new plural handling for keys matching `/(.+)_id(s?)$/` does `obj[k].map(...)` without checking that `obj[k]` is a non-null array. If a payload includes `foo_ids: null` (or any non-array), hydration will throw a `TypeError` on `null.map`. Also, unlike the singular branch which only assigns/deletes when `hydrated` is truthy, the plural branch always assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` and deletes the raw `*_ids`, even if `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined` for some ids, yielding arrays containing `undefined` and losing the original ids. The added JS tests only cover the all-ids-present case (`color_ids` with `colors` side-loaded) and do not exercise lookup-miss/null cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The fabricator files are content-swapped: category_fabricator.rb now defines only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while all four category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category) were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Fabrication loads files by glob so the suite still passes, but the next developer who edits or deletes embeddable_host_fabricator.rb (believing it holds the embeddable host fabricator) removes the category fabricators and breaks the entire spec suite, and anyone searching for the :category definition is sent to the wrong file.
matched_golden_ids: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly states that category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb have had their contents swapped (category file defines embeddable_host; category fabricators moved to the embeddable host file), which is the same underlying issue as the golden comment and notes the risk of losing/ breaking category fabricators.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only spec covering Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts class inheritance and never exercises create, update, destroy, or save_host. The guard is a pure proxy that stays green no matter what the actions do — any regression in the new CRUD surface (the uncategorized defaulting, the error rendering, a mistyped params key) passes CI and ships to the first staff user in production.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new CRUD controller `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` with nontrivial behavior in `save_host` (assigning `host` and `category_id` from `params[:embeddable_host]`, defaulting blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, and branching between `render_serialized` vs `render_json_error`). However, the only added spec (`spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb`) merely asserts it subclasses `Admin::AdminController` and does not exercise `create`, `update`, `destroy`, or the `save_host` logic. That means regressions in this new admin CRUD surface would not be caught by CI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The referer check on the embed/comments hot path changed from a cached in-process SiteSetting read to an unconditional per-request SQL query — EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? runs `where("lower(host) = ?")` against a column with no index. Every render of an embedded comments iframe now adds a database roundtrip (a non-sargable full scan) where the previous check cost zero DB reads, adding load that scales with embed traffic on popular sites.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the embed hot-path referer check to call `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (e.g., `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb` and `lib/topic_retriever.rb`). `host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host`, which performs a SQL lookup: `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (in `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`). The new migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates the `embeddable_hosts` table without adding any index on `host` (`db/migrate/...create_embeddable_hosts.rb`), and the use of `lower(host)` means a plain index on `host` (even if added later) wouldn’t be used without a functional index. This is a concrete per-request DB roundtrip/perf regression concern, but not a functional correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The host format regex requires a dotted TLD of exactly 2-5 letters (`\.[a-z]{2,5}`), rejecting dotless hostnames like 'localhost' or 'intranet' and valid 6-character TLDs like '.museum'. An admin whose embedding origin is a dotless internal hostname or a long-TLD domain cannot whitelist it — the save is rejected with a format error and there is no workaround short of the development-mode admin bypass.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` with `validates_format_of :host, with: /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). After `before_validation` strips protocol and paths, saving a host like `localhost`/`intranet` (no dot) or a domain with a >5-letter TLD (e.g. `.museum`) will fail validation and thus be rejected by `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` which calls `host.save` and errors otherwise. This is a concrete, diff-grounded behavior regression/defect for legitimate hostnames/TLDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration raises NoMethodError on nil because `execute(...)[0]` is nil when the `embed_category` setting has no site_settings row or its value no longer matches a category name, and the `if category_id == 0` fallback to uncategorized_category_id is unreachable dead code (Postgres category ids are never 0 and the crash happens before the branch). Every fresh install and every existing site that never customized embed_category fails `db:migrate` with `undefined method '[]' for nil:NilClass`, blocking the entire deploy; the written intent — default migrated hosts to the uncategorized category — is never executed.

adjudication.rationale: In migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, `category_id = execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` assumes the SELECT for the `embed_category` site_setting returns at least one row. If no matching row exists (e.g., no `site_settings` row for `embed_category`, or value doesn’t match any category name), `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `['id']` raises `NoMethodError`. The subsequent `if category_id == 0` fallback is not reached in that case, so the intended uncategorized fallback won’t execute.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts setting entries verbatim via raw SQL, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation scheme/path stripping, so entries like `http://eviltrout.com` — which the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` explicitly accepted (it stripped the scheme before comparing, per the specs this diff deletes) — are stored with the `http://` prefix intact. After upgrade, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against the bare referer host from `uri.host`, so a migrated `http://example.com` row never matches and every embed request from that host returns InvalidAccess — existing embeds break silently across the site with no error and no migration warning.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` inserts legacy hosts via raw SQL (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) without running `EmbeddableHost` validations/callbacks. The `EmbeddableHost` model’s `before_validation` is what strips `http(s)://` and paths, but it won’t run for these inserts. Meanwhile `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the request URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` against the bare `uri.host`. If a migrated row is stored as `http://eviltrout.com`, it will not match `eviltrout.com`, so `host_allowed?` returns false and embeds will be rejected post-upgrade for those legacy entries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `update` and `destroy` feed `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` directly into `save_host`/`destroy` with no nil check, so any request for a nonexistent host id raises NoMethodError on nil (`nil.host =` in save_host, `nil.destroy` in destroy). PUT or DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale id (the host was already deleted from another admin session or tab) returns a 500 instead of a 404, and because the client delete flow has no rejection handler the row silently stays in the table.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without handling `nil` (nonexistent id). `save_host` does `host.host = ...`, which will raise `NoMethodError` if `host` is nil, and `destroy` will likewise raise on `nil.destroy`, producing a 500 instead of a 404. On the client side, the component `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch(...)`, so a failed delete would not be surfaced and the row would remain.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` on every embed request, replacing the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` read that was served from Discourse's per-process settings cache, and the migration creates no index on `host` (which the `lower()` wrap would defeat anyway). Every pageview of every externally embedding site now incurs a per-request sequential-scan DB query on the /embed/comments hot path — externally driven traffic the forum cannot throttle — so database load scales with third-party pageviews where it previously scaled at zero.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the cached SiteSetting-based allowlist check with a DB-backed check on the hot embed path: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` now calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` which calls `record_for_host` and executes `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` for every request. The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` without any index on `host`, and the `lower(host)` predicate would not use a plain index anyway. This is a concrete performance/scaling concern introduced by the change, not a functional correctness break visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The fabricator files have their contents swapped: category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while all 27 lines of :category/:diff_category/:happy_category/:private_category fabricators moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb (the new file's blob hash a37f5b4c8ba is identical to the old category_fabricator.rb, proving an accidental swap). Tests keep passing because Fabricator globs the whole directory, but maintainers navigating by filename edit the wrong file, git blame/history for the category fabricators is severed, and a future partial revert or `git mv` of either file silently drops or duplicates fabricator definitions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was replaced to define only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while a new file `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the full set of category-related fabricators that previously lived in `category_fabricator.rb` (the content matches the removed block). This is not a runtime defect if the test suite autoloads all fabricators, but it is a concrete maintainability/review issue: filenames no longer match their contents, and history/blame for category fabricators is effectively moved to the wrong file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `update` action persists nothing — it re-renders the same OpenStruct from fetch_embedding — and its only client caller, `saveChanges` in admin-embedding.js.es6, is triggered by no element in embedding.hbs, leaving the PUT /admin/customize/embedding route and the controller action inert. A future developer wiring embedding-level settings to this page will assume the existing save plumbing works and ship a UI that silently discards user input, because the endpoint returns a success-shaped payload without saving anything.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` without mutating anything (the model is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`), so the PUT endpoint can’t persist changes. On the client, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({})`, but `admin/templates/embedding.hbs` contains no element invoking `saveChanges`, so the PUT route/action are currently unused/inert. This isn’t a user-facing defect yet because there are no embedding-level editable fields shown, but it is a diff-grounded maintainability trap: the presence of a PUT route + controller action that always returns a success-shaped payload could mislead future work into assuming save plumbing exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The migration deletes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site-setting rows inside `change` with no down path, destroying the source data irreversibly while `create_table` remains auto-reversible. An operator who rolls back this migration to back out a bad release gets the table dropped but the deleted settings rows are not restored — the site's entire embeddable-host configuration is lost with no recovery path.

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration is defined with `def change` (auto-reversible for `create_table`), but it also performs irreversible data mutations via raw SQL, notably `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. On rollback, Rails will drop `embeddable_hosts` table but cannot restore the deleted `site_settings` rows because no `down`/`reversible` block is provided, resulting in configuration data loss when rolling back.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The validation regex explicitly accepts port-bearing hosts via `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`, but `record_for_host` matches against `uri.host`, which never includes a port, so a stored `example.com:8080` can never equal any referer host. An admin who whitelists `example.com:8080` gets a clean save and then embedding from that host keeps failing with InvalidAccess and no diagnostic — the model accepts input its own matching logic cannot honor.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, `validates_format_of :host` explicitly allows an optional port via `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` (and `before_validation` does not remove ports; it only strips `http(s)://` and any `/...` path). However `record_for_host(host)` parses the referer with `URI(host)` and matches using `host = uri.host`, which never includes the port, then queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. Therefore a saved record like `example.com:8080` can never match any referer, even `http://example.com:8080/...`, because it will be looked up as `example.com`. This makes a port-bearing whitelist entry silently ineffective, leading to `InvalidAccess` failures as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The delete action chains `destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch`, unlike the save action in the same component that handles rejection with popupAjaxError. When the DELETE fails (the 500 from the unguarded nil host in the controller, or a stale-id rejection), the admin gets no feedback and the row remains in the table, so the failure presents as the confirm dialog doing nothing.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action does `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` with no rejection handling, unlike `save()` which has `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. If the DELETE request fails, there is no user feedback and no state rollback. This failure is plausible from the diff because `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately calls `host.destroy` without guarding against `nil`, which can raise and produce a 500. In that case, `deleteHost` is never sent, so the row stays and the confirm appears to do nothing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only spec for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts subclass ancestry, leaving the new `save_host` logic — the blank-category fallback to uncategorized_category_id, validation-error rendering, and the before_validation host normalization — with no test coverage. A regression in the uncategorized fallback or the error path ships with no failing spec, and embedded topics start posting to the wrong category or the controller returns unrendered 500s on invalid input.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial controller logic in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` (blank `category_id` fallback to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, and error handling via `render_json_error` on failed `host.save`). However, `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` only asserts the controller inherits from `Admin::AdminController` and does not exercise `create/update/destroy` or `save_host`. While there is model coverage for host normalization in `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb` (trimming http/https/paths), the controller paths and fallback behavior are untested, making the review concern specific and diff-grounded but not a currently verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `belongs_to :category` has no dependent handling and nothing in the diff or in category deletion cleans up embeddable_hosts rows, leaving dangling category_id values after a category is deleted. Once an admin deletes a category that hosts point at, the embedding table renders a blank category, the next host save silently reassigns the host to uncategorized, and TopicEmbed.import passes the dead category_id to PostCreator for newly embedded topics.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` with `belongs_to :category` and a non-null `category_id` column (migration `create_table :embeddable_hosts ... t.integer :category_id, null: false`) but shows no foreign key, no `dependent:` handling, and no category-deletion cleanup. As a result, deleting a category can leave orphaned `embeddable_hosts.category_id` values. This can surface in multiple places added/changed here: admin UI renders `{{category-badge host.category}}` and the component’s `edit()` reads `this.get('host.category.id')` (can be nil if the category no longer exists / can’t be hydrated), and `TopicEmbed.import` now uses `category: eh.try(:category_id)` which would pass a stale/dead category id when the referenced category has been deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration string-interpolates each line of the migrated embeddable_hosts site setting directly into a raw SQL INSERT (VALUES ('#{h}', ...)), so a stored value containing a single quote breaks out of the string literal and injects arbitrary SQL. The old embeddable_hosts setting was free-form admin-entered text with no write-side format validation (the removed allows_embeddable_host? only stripped schemes at read time, and the removed specs show values like 'http://discourse.org' being stored), so any value with an apostrophe aborts db:migrate with a PG syntax error and blocks the upgrade; a deliberately crafted setting value (config treated as attacker input) executes attacker-chosen SQL with the migration role's privileges during deploy.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Since `h` comes from the existing `site_settings` row `embeddable_hosts` (free-form text in prior versions) and is not escaped/quoted safely, any value containing a single quote will break the SQL and can potentially inject arbitrary SQL during migration. This is a real, diff-verifiable correctness/security issue that could block upgrades.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] update passes the unchecked result of EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first into save_host, so a request whose id matches no row executes nil.host = ... and raises NoMethodError. An admin saving a host that another admin deleted in the meantime (or any direct PUT to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a bogus id) gets a 500 from an unhandled NoMethodError instead of a 404, and the Ember client's save flow surfaces a raw server error.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. `save_host` immediately dereferences `host` (`host.host = ...`, `host.category_id = ...`), so if the record isn’t found `host` is `nil` and a `NoMethodError` will be raised, returning a 500 instead of a 404. The same nil-deref risk also exists in `#destroy` (`host.destroy` without checking `host`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] destroy calls host.destroy on the unchecked result of EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first, raising NoMethodError on nil when the id matches no row. A DELETE for an already-removed host (double-click on the trash button racing the first request, or two admins managing hosts simultaneously) returns a 500 instead of success_json/404, rejecting the client's destroyRecord promise and leaving the row stuck in the UI.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `host.destroy`. If no row matches the id, `host` is `nil` and this will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 instead of a graceful 404/success response. The diff shows no nil handling, so the finding is directly verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host] without any require/permit guard, so a create or update request whose payload omits the embeddable_host key raises NoMethodError on nil[:host]. Any direct POST/PUT to /admin/embeddable_hosts without the embeddable_host payload (an API consumer or client bug) returns a 500 instead of a 400, logging an unhandled exception on an admin route.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code directly dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` (new file `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`, lines in `save_host`). If the request omits the `embeddable_host` key, `params[:embeddable_host]` will be `nil` and `nil[:host]` will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 rather than a handled client error. The diff shows no `require`/guard/strong-params handling to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The before_validation block calls self.host.sub! with no nil guard, so saving a record whose host attribute is nil raises NoMethodError before validates_format_of can reject the value. Creating a host with an embeddable_host payload that omits the host key (host.host = nil) returns a 500 instead of the 422 validation error that the controller's render_json_error branch is designed to produce.
matched_golden_ids: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the before_validation callback calls `self.host.sub!` without checking for nil, so when `host` is nil it raises `NoMethodError` instead of allowing validations to handle it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] category_id is accepted from params with no existence validation, the new embeddable_hosts table has no foreign key, and nothing clears embeddable_hosts.category_id when a category is deleted, so an EmbeddableHost row can reference a nonexistent category. An admin deletes a category that an embeddable host posts to; every subsequent feed-poll import (TopicEmbed.import passes eh.category_id straight to PostCreator) then creates embedded topics against a category that no longer exists, silently misfiling or breaking those topics.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces EmbeddableHost.category_id persisted in a new table (migration creates `embeddable_hosts` with `category_id, null: false`) but does not add a foreign key or any existence validation. The controller accepts `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` and only substitutes uncategorized when blank, not when the referenced category is missing. If a category is deleted, `embeddable_hosts.category_id` can point to a nonexistent record; `TopicEmbed.import` then passes `eh.try(:category_id)` straight into `PostCreator` (with `skip_validations: true`), and the admin UI also assumes `host.category` exists (`edit()` does `this.get('host.category.id')`). This is a real, diff-grounded correctness issue caused by missing referential integrity/handling for deleted categories.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The only test in this new spec asserts `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`, which passes regardless of what the controller's actions do, so create/update/destroy ship with zero behavioral verification. A regression in any controller behavior passes CI: update and destroy crash with NoMethodError (500) when params[:id] matches no EmbeddableHost (nil is passed to save_host/destroy), and the blank-category_id fallback to uncategorized_category_id is never exercised — an admin acting on a stale/deleted row gets an unhandled 500 with no failing test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` where `update` and `destroy` fetch a host via `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without handling the `nil` case. If no record matches `params[:id]`, `save_host` will raise `NoMethodError` on `host.host = ...`, and `destroy` will raise on `host.destroy`, producing an unhandled 500. The new controller spec indeed only asserts subclassing and does not cover these behaviors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The only test asserts `Admin::EmbeddingController < Admin::AdminController` and never issues a request, so the show/update serialization contract that the new JS store hydration depends on is completely unverified. The payload shape the new _hydrateEmbedded plural-ids path consumes (root 'embedding' with embeddable_host_ids side-load) has no test — if the serializer emits a shape the store mishandles, the admin embedding page renders an empty hosts table with CI green; the update action, which persists nothing (it only re-renders the OpenStruct built in fetch_embedding), also ships unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new admin endpoints/serializers (`Admin::EmbeddingController#show/#update`, `EmbeddingSerializer` with `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids`) and client-side hydration changes in `store.js.es6` to support plural `*_ids`, but the only Ruby controller specs added (`spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` and `.../embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb`) merely assert inheritance and do not exercise any request/response payload shape. There is also no request/spec coverage confirming the `root: 'embedding'` + `embeddable_host_ids`/sideload contract that the new JS admin embedding page relies on. This is a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap rather than a directly verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The restructured expandable_first_post? tests still treat embeddable hosts as a gating input even though this diff removed the host check from the method: the 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false and has_topic_embed? is false on a built topic, and every positive test fabricates an EmbeddableHost the code never reads.
